summary.one_liner: ripgrep (rg) is a fast, line-oriented command-line search tool that recursively searches directories for regex patterns, respecting gitignore rules by default.
summary.what_it_does: Recursively searches the current directory for a regex pattern and skips hidden files, binary files, and paths matched by .gitignore, .ignore, or .rgignore by default (disable with rg -uuu). Supports file-type filters such as -tpy and -Tjs, context lines, multiple patterns, color, and full Unicode. Optional PCRE2 regex engine (-P/--pcre2 or --auto-hybrid-regex) adds look-around and backreferences. It can search non-UTF-8 encodings via -E/--encoding, search compressed files (brotli, bzip2, gzip, lz4, lzma, xz, zstandard) with -z, run input preprocessing filters, and read a configuration file. The README includes benchmarks against ag, ack, git grep, ugrep and GNU grep.
use_cases: search source code for a pattern
find text in a large directory tree while ignoring gitignored files
search only files of a given type
search files in UTF-16 or other non-UTF-8 encodings
search with look-around or backreference regex
how_to_run: git clone https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep && cd ripgrep && cargo build --release
notable: Respects .gitignore/.ignore/.rgignore and skips hidden and binary files by default
Optional PCRE2 engine for look-around and backreferences via -P or --auto-hybrid-regex
Searches compressed files (gzip, xz, zstd, etc.) with -z
Chooses memory-map or buffered search strategy automatically
Binary downloads for Windows, macOS and Linux; packaged in many distros
caveats: Not POSIX or ubiquitous; the README says grep remains the portable choice
PCRE2 support is opt-in and requires a feature build flag
Minimum supported Rust version is 1.96.0 for building from source
